# Architecture

> **2.0 approved target, not yet implemented:** [ADR-0001](decisions/ADR-0001-MODULAR-COMPANION-APKS.md) commits to a Full-only Launcher APK plus independently installed optional companion APKs, with a Launcher-led installer and verified data migration. See [staged roadmap](2.0/MODULARIZATION_ROADMAP.md), [distribution spec](2.0/COMPANION_DISTRIBUTION.md) and [PR127 handoff](2.0/PR127_HANDOFF.md). The module layout and embedded extras described below are **the current codebase**, not the new destination. Keep the historical technical details for recovery until the corresponding extraction is complete.

Current behavior: 1.0.0 preparation. Dated acceptance sections below retain historical context.

## Modules

```text
:app      application, io.github.aimindseye.tenseven (Compose UI, activities, repositories, generated Tabler glyphs)
:design   library, io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.design (theme, tokens, shared components, string tables), used by :app
```

`:app` contains the Sable Start source tree, the activities included, plus Tenseven's own code (BlackBerry 7 home,
Launcher Settings, default-app lookup, sound control, extra apps). SableOS builds the Sable files as
`SableLauncher` with its Android.bp (system SDK); Tenseven builds them with Gradle against the public SDK, so
anything that needs a system API is isolated behind a small helper (below).

### Source layout inside `:app`

Directory `app/src/main/java/io/github/aimindseye/tenseven` (packages renamed from upstream `org.sableos.start`):

| Directory | Package | What |
|---|---|---|
| `model/` | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.model` | Pure Kotlin policy, unit tested: home styles and layouts, app glyphs, quick bar, letter shortcuts, speed dial, command queries, Hub bar, text tables |
| `privacy/` | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.privacy` | The All Apps privacy row: the evaluator, summary policy and snapshot cache (pure Kotlin) |
| `platform/` | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.platform` | Android access: `LauncherAppsRepository`, `RecentTasksRepository`, `StartStateRepository`, `LiveSurfaceRepository`, `PeopleRepository`, `UsageRecentsRepository` (recent apps from usage events), `PrivacyFactsReader`, `DeviceStatsSampler`, and Tenseven's `PermissionChangeSignal` and `UserContexts` |
| `onboarding/` | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.onboarding` | Setup: `OnboardingPlan` (step order and when to explain Allow restricted settings, pure and tested) and `SetupStatus` (what is granted); the screen is `OnboardingActivity` |
| `iconpacks/` | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.iconpacks` | Nova and ADW icon packs: discovery, `appfilter` parsing, drawable loading; `IconPacks` holds the chosen pack (Appearance) and `loadLauncherIcon` uses it; mapping rules are pure and tested; ported from Mink |
| `conversations/` | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.conversations` | Notification access: `ConversationListenerService` reads message and email notifications into `ConversationHub` (in memory only); feeds the Hub bar counts; ported from Mink, see `third_party/minklauncher/PORTING.md` |
| `ui/` | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.ui` | Compose: `SableStartScreen` (BlackBerry 10 home, Hub, Command, All Apps), `Bb7HomeScreen` (BlackBerry 7 home, tray, menu), `SoundProfileButton`, `LineIcon` (Tabler-style line icons drawn from path data), glyphs and status rings |
| `live/` | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.live` | Models for the live tiles (calendar, mail, media) |
| `extras/` | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.extras` | Optional apps ported from SableOS: Calc Plus, Notes and Sound Profiles. Their manifest entries are disabled with their own task affinity; `ExtraAppsControl` switches them on. Each has its own palette and strings so it does not touch the launcher's |
| (root) | `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven` | `SableStartActivity` (HOME, both layouts, the BlackBerry 10 detour), `HomeStyleActivity`, `LauncherSettingsActivity` and `SettingsSections` (the setting groups shared with Setup), `HubSettingsActivity`, `LockLayerActivity`, `BackupActivity`, `OnboardingActivity`, `LauncherTheme` |

Tenseven-only files worth knowing: `model/GridColumns`, `model/HubApps`, `model/LockLayer`, `model/ThemePresets` (themes and `WallpaperSets`), `model/WidgetList`, `platform/WidgetHostController`, `platform/WallpaperArt`, `platform/LockLayerLauncher` and `LockLayerState`, `platform/RecentLaunchesRepository`, `ui/WidgetsPage`, `ui/HubPeek`, `model/Bb7Home` (panels, grid maths), `model/LauncherSettings` (icon sizes, which widgets can be switched), `model/HomeLayout` (`GlanceWidgets`), `model/RingerProfile` (sound-mode cycle), `platform/DefaultApps` (finds the phone's own dialer, messages, mail, camera, calendar, browser, gallery and music apps), `platform/SoundProfileControl`, `platform/NextAlarm`.

### Two home layouts, one activity

`SableStartActivity` hosts both layouts in a pager (Widgets page, Hub, Home, app grid pages). The BlackBerry 7 layout is chosen in Launcher Settings. Command and Hub are BlackBerry 10 surfaces, so from BlackBerry 7 they open as a **detour**: `startBb10Detour(returnOnHome)` shows the BlackBerry 10 view, and `endBb10Detour()` returns once the user is back on Home, when the app goes to the background (`onPause`) or when Back is pressed on the Hub (`onBackToHomePage`). That ordering is what prevents a flash of the BlackBerry 10 screen when switching. The window is translucent so the BlackBerry 7 banner and tray sit over the wallpaper.

### Widgets page

`StartPages.WIDGETS` is the page left of Hub; when the page is on, every pager index is the page's own number plus one (`lead` in `SableStartScreen`). `WidgetHostController` wraps `AppWidgetHost`: allocate id, bind (Android's permission screen the first time), run the widget's setup screen, save the id (`StartStateRepository`, never backed up). The activity forwards `onActivityResult` and starts/stops listening in `onStart`/`onStop`. `ui/WidgetsPage` draws each widget in an `AndroidView` at the height it asks for (`WidgetSizing`); list policy is `model/WidgetList`. From the BlackBerry 7 home it is a detour like Hub (`widgetsGeneration`).

### Widgets: the page, and nothing on the home

One `WidgetHostController` (one `AppWidgetHost` id) serves the Widgets page (`WidgetTarget.PAGE`). The `HOME` target and `home_widget_ids` are kept for old saves. BB10 Active Frames can show available TenSeven-owned Calendar/Now playing summaries, but do not embed arbitrary third-party widgets. The built-in widgets (`GlanceWidgets`: Calendar, Alarm, Battery, Now playing; none on by default, switched in Launcher Settings) are drawn by `BuiltInWidgets` as the top of the Widgets page, passed into `WidgetsPage` as its `builtIn` slot. Edit mode dims an added widget and puts Up, Down, Shorter, Taller and Remove in a row under it. Edit Home ends in a bar that stays on screen (`EditBar`: Reset, Cancel, Done).

### Settings groups shared with Setup

`SettingsSections.kt` holds one composable per Launcher Settings group (`HomeStyleSection`, `IconGridSection`, `ThemeSection`, `WallpaperSection`, `WidgetsSection`, `HubSection`, `LockLayerSection`). Each reads and saves its own choices through `StartStateRepository`, draws no heading, and is used by both `LauncherSettingsActivity` and `OnboardingActivity`. Setup has a choice step (`SetupStep.isChoice`) for each group: always offered, never "not done", applied at once. `OnboardingPlanTest` fails if the choice steps and the groups drift apart. To add a setting: put it in a section, and add a step if it is a new group.

### Themes, wallpapers and the home backdrop

`LauncherTheme` replaces `SableGlobalTheme` in every Tenseven activity: the theme chosen in Launcher Settings (`appearance_mode`, `appearance_accent`, backed up) wins when set; otherwise the Sable global provider is read, which only exists on SableOS. `ThemePresets` and `WallpaperSets` are pure models (unit tested). `WallpaperArt` paints each wallpaper in code (gradient, soft disc, layered ridges, seeded per set), so no image files ship, and sets it through `WallpaperManager` for Home, Lock or both (`SET_WALLPAPER`). The BlackBerry 7 home always draws on the wallpaper; the BlackBerry 10 home does so when `home_wallpaper` is on (default), by showing the wallpaper window flag and painting its background at 60% (`LocalHomeBackdrop`).

### Hub controls and the peek

`HubUnifiedNavigation` renders all ten category/utility actions in one horizontally scrolling
row. Actual window width determines how many fit, independent of device-brand guesses;
buttons retain their minimum 48 dp touch target. Per-app notification icons belong to Home,
where selecting one opens the matching Hub source filter. The peek uses rounded corners.


`ConversationListenerService` drops notifications from apps in `hub_excluded_apps` (`HubApps`) before they reach `ConversationHub`; `ConversationHub.clearNow()` is the "Clear the Hub now" button. Nothing about message text is persisted. `hub_peek_text` (off by default) decides whether the lock layer and the peek may show the latest message. The peek (`ui/HubPeek`) is an overlay on the BlackBerry 10 Start destination; a pointer handler on the Initial pass opens it from a drag that starts in the left 20 dp of Home and consumes the rest of that drag so the pager does not also move.

### Lock layer

The system keyguard cannot be replaced by a launcher, so the lock layer is a cover: `LockLayerActivity` is `showWhenLocked` and `turnScreenOn`, in its own task, with a translucent wallpaper theme. `ConversationListenerService` registers for `ACTION_SCREEN_ON` while notification access is connected and calls `LockLayerLauncher.showIfLocked`, which needs the setting on, `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` granted and the keyguard up; it shows a one-pixel overlay window around `startActivity` because Android 14+ only allows a background start while the app has a visible window. Counts come from `LockLayer.tally` over the active notifications (never their text). Unlocking calls `KeyguardManager.requestDismissKeyguard`, so the real lock is always what lets the user in; the camera uses the secure camera intent. A preview from Settings or Setup carries `EXTRA_RETURN_TO` and returns to the screen it came from.

### Default apps, not Sable apps

Starting icons, BlackBerry 10 tiles, Hub actions and the Mail, Calendar and Music glance cards resolve through `DefaultApps` (category intents, the default SMS and dialer roles, an image-capture intent) and need `<queries>` entries for package visibility. Nothing requires a Sable app. There is no weather tile: Tenseven makes no network requests, so the only route to live weather is hosting an Android widget (the Widgets page above).

### Settings and storage

Preferences live in `StartStateRepository` (SharedPreferences). `LauncherBackup.ALLOWED` lists the keys a backup may hold; `LauncherBackupTest` fails if the two sets differ, so adding a preference means adding it to both. Booleans are stored as numbers 0/1.

### Sound

`SoundProfileControl` reads and sets `AudioManager.ringerMode`. Silent and vibrate-only need Do Not Disturb access (`ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY`); changing tones, vibration and light in Sound Profiles needs `WRITE_SETTINGS`. Without access the button skips Silent rather than failing. The Sound Profiles extra opens from a tap on the speaker when it is switched on; a long press cycles quickly.

Rule that makes this testable: decisions live in `model/` and `privacy/` with unit tests; `platform/` and
`ui/` only gather facts and draw. Keep it that way for anything added.

## Features that need the system, and what an ordinary install does

SableOS gives Sable Start signature permissions because the launcher is platform-signed. An ordinary install
cannot hold them, so each such feature has a fallback, and the Mink port named in the last column is what
replaces the missing data.

| Feature | On SableOS | Ordinary install today | Plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active Frames: list and live pictures of recent apps | `ActivityManager` recents plus hidden `IActivityTaskManager` calls (`READ_FRAME_BUFFER`, `REAL_GET_TASKS`) | Recent apps from launches and usage stats as icon cards in the same frame grid (usage access adds apps opened elsewhere) | Done |
| Close a frame (X / Backspace) | Dismiss TenSeven card only | Dismiss TenSeven card only, persisted | Safe default in P2-B |
| Recents key opens Active Frames | The system's Recents is redirected to `SHOW_ACTIVE_FRAMES` | Android keeps its own Recents; SableOS's key notes report the system opens its Overview even when an accessibility service consumes the key | A home key or letter opens Active Frames |
| Runtime-permission changes refresh the privacy rows | `OnPermissionsChangedListener` (system API) | `PermissionChangeSignal.register()` returns false; rows refresh on package events only | Refresh when returning to Home |
| Privacy row for work and private profile apps | `createContextAsUser` for that profile | `UserContexts.forUser` returns null; the row says "permissions · unavailable" | Accept; document |
| Lock and unlock Private Space | `MODIFY_QUIET_MODE` | Android decides whether a non-system launcher may do it; the call is already wrapped, so a refusal leaves the space as it was | Mink Private Space port; test on Android 15+ |
| Hub (messages, calls, contacts, notifications) | Sable Hub, Messages and Phone publish snapshot providers | Notification-based Hub (Mink conversations), in memory only | Done |
| Watch (Sable Watch) | Sable Hub, Calendar and Weather providers, read by Sable Watch directly | `HubCountsProvider` (`io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.hubcounts/apps`): the Hub bar's per-app counts, no text, behind the signature permission `READ_HUB_COUNTS`, so only a same-key app reads it; nothing while notification access is off | Implemented; production-signed Watch/Titan 2 acceptance pending |
| Appearance (theme, accent) | Settings hosts `org.sableos.appearance` | Launcher's own preferences (Launcher Settings): `LauncherTheme` uses the saved choice when there is one and the Sable provider otherwise; `ThemePresets` and `WallpaperSets` are pure models | Done |
| Lock layer | Not applicable (the phone's keyguard is Android's) | `LockLayerActivity` (show-when-locked cover, started on screen-on by the notification listener when the overlay permission is granted); it never replaces the keyguard and asks Android to dismiss it before opening anything | Written, not yet run on a phone |
| Speed dial | Sable Phone provider and `org.sableos.permission.SPEED_DIAL` | Not available; letter shortcuts for apps still work | Launcher-owned letter-to-contact map |
| Live tiles: calendar, mail, media | Sable app providers | The phone's default apps; calendar entries via `READ_CALENDAR`, Now Playing via notification access | Done; weather removed (see above) |

The SableOS build of the same sources keeps the manifest and Android.bp in the SableOS repository; the
ordinary-install manifest is `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, and `tests/run.sh` fails if it ever asks for
a signature permission.

## Icons

`AppGlyph` entries name Tabler outline icons (`AppGlyphs.kt`). `tools/tabler_icons.py` copies the SVGs from the
pinned npm package into `third_party/tabler-icons/`, writes `TablerGlyphPaths.kt` (one path string per SVG
element; elements are never joined, because a relative moveto starts from the previous element's last point)
and the adaptive launcher icon. `SableGlyphIcon` strokes those paths (width 2 in a 24-unit box, round caps and
joins) under the Sable lighting: white shading to an accent-tinted silver, over a soft shadow. An app that has
no glyph draws its own icon (its themed monochrome layer when it has one). Third-party app logos are covered in
[`BRAND_ASSETS.md`](BRAND_ASSETS.md).

## Key profiles

Sable Start reads keys by Android key code. The devices differ in what the trackpad sends (D-pad keys or a
pointer), where Sym, Menu and the convenience key are, and whether Alt-plus-letter gives a digit. A key profile
records those facts per device so the shortcuts can be trusted. Capture with `adb shell getevent -lt` or the
event viewer in Sable Keyboard, then add a row here:

| Device | Keyboard name (`InputDevice`) | Trackpad | Sym | Menu | Convenience key | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Zinwa Q25 | `Q25_keyboard` | D-pad keys (kernel mode 1) or pointer (mode 0); SableOS wants D-pad | Right Alt | `KEYCODE_MENU` (kl 139) | scan code unknown | no |
| Zinwa P26 | not captured | not captured | not captured | not captured | not captured | no |
| Unihertz Titan 2 | not captured | Touch-sensitive keyboard (not captured in detail) | not captured | No Menu key: Alt+Enter opens the menu | not captured | Alt+Space (Command) and Alt+Enter (menu) work in hand testing |

The Q25 row is from SableOS's `device-profile/KEYMAP.md` and `docs/KEYBOARD_AND_INPUT.md` (device tree and
kernel source, not measured on hardware).

## Sable Keyboard (companion app, separate)

Sable Keyboard is an input method (about 4,800 lines of Kotlin with unit tests, no permissions, works before first
unlock) with per-device Alt layers, AutoText, a candidate strip and optional clipboard history. It stays a
**separate APK** from the launcher:

- A keyboard sees everything you type. Keeping its permission list empty is its privacy promise; merging it into
  a launcher that holds contacts and notification access would break it.
- Updates and crashes of one must not restart the other, and people use one without the other.
- The two cooperate without depending on each other: on first run the launcher offers the system keyboard
  picker, and type-to-find on Home works with any keyboard.

To make it standalone: lower `minSdk` from 36 to 30 and find the calls that need 36; detect the device from the
keyboard it reports (`InputDevice`, model) instead of the `ro.sable.profile.id` property, with a manual choice
in settings; read the accent from its own preference when the SableOS appearance provider is absent; and give
it its own package and signature. Its layouts for Titan 2 and Q25 are marked unverified upstream.

## Backup, quick actions and the lock service

- `model/LauncherBackup` is the backup format: JSON with `format`, `version` and an allow-list of preference keys. A file with an unknown key, a wrong type or another version is refused whole, before anything changes. `BackupActivity` uses the system file picker, so no storage permission is requested. Restoring replaces the listed settings and restarts the launcher. Not included: setup state, letter shortcuts and speed dial (they hold contact names), permissions.
- `model/QuickActions` parses `-` (to-do), `/` (note) and `+` (event) in Command and recognises web addresses. To-dos and notes go to an app the user picks through the share sheet; events open the calendar's own new-event screen. Tenseven keeps nothing.
- `LockScreenAccessibilityService` is declared with no event types, no window content and no gestures. Double-tap detection sits on empty Home space only (tiles and rows consume their own taps). **Google Play:** an accessibility service that is not an accessibility tool must be declared and justified in Play Console; review that policy before any Play release. GitHub and F-Droid builds are not affected.


## Reminder and notification recovery boundaries

`tasks/TaskRepository` owns durable task changes, deduplication and repeat completion. It takes a
`TaskStore`, `TaskScheduler` and clock so these policies can be exercised with real temporary storage
and a recording scheduler in JVM tests. `tasks/TaskSchedule` owns timezone calculations, including
Android-11-compatible local-date conversion. `platform/TaskPlatform` wires the repository to Android
alarm and notification APIs. The registered `tasks.TaskAlarmReceiver` component delegates to that
adapter, preserving existing alarm identity and stored task files.

`conversations/NotificationRecoveryController` owns permission transitions, throttling, retry generations
and the bounded recovery sequence. Its tests simulate delayed grants, permission loss, stale callbacks
and already-connected listeners. `platform/NotificationConnectionRecovery` only supplies the Android
handler, elapsed clock and application context. `NotificationConnection` keeps the observable counts-only
status used by the UI. No Activity context is retained by recovery timers.

These Android adapters follow the existing platform coverage policy. The task domain and recovery
controller remain in the measured sources and have regression tests; no new coverage exclusions or
quality-gate thresholds were introduced. CI now reports Sonar gate conditions and source findings using
the existing Sonar credential, without exporting it, while the scanner continues to enforce the gate.

## P2-B Active Frames boundary

`ui/ActiveFramesPage.kt` owns the frame page, two-column grid, focus recovery,
card rendering and explicit Recent app / Preview / Live tile presentation. It
receives `FramesState` and callbacks; no binder task query or dismissal store is
owned by a composable. `SableStartScreen` routes the page; `SableStartActivity`
forwards lifecycle and app/profile invalidation to `platform/ActiveFramesHost`.

`frames/FramesCoordinator` owns resume/stop/destroy epochs, stale-result rejection,
immediate dismissal, and safe open decisions. `FramePolicy` merges incomplete
native tasks with launcher/Usage history, using exact package/profile identities
and stable keys. Per-card dismissal timestamps survive process recreation without hiding another task for the same app; a
newer personal foreground event or explicit exact-profile launcher launch can
restore a card. Metadata is bounded to 96 dismissals. No snapshots are persisted.
An unavailable or paused/private profile cannot fall back to another user's copy.

`ActiveFramesHost` binds a single background executor to Android repositories and
publishes on the main dispatcher. Its one-worker/one-pending-task queue drops obsolete pending reads during inventory bursts. Task resume is performed off the UI thread;
normal app launch is dispatched to the host UI thread. Pause and stop invalidate pending
work and clears frame/image presentation. Destroy shuts down the executor.
Snapshots are loaded only for composed cards, only while active and authorized,
with stale completion rejection, closed HardwareBuffers and a 512-pixel bound.
Android's non-real theme snapshots are not labelled Preview. The OS retains its
secure-content restrictions. A separate, explicitly consented MediaProjection session is described below.

The pure `PlatformCapabilities` contract and Android `PlatformCapabilityProbe`
are shared by frame settings and `RecentTasksRepository` operations. Native task
queries, resume and snapshots require detected grants (and bridge methods where
needed), not device models or a nonempty partial task result. The normal Full APK
requests no signature permissions. Close always dismisses the TenSeven card; it
never invokes removeTask or force-stop. The underlying app remains intact.

`FrameSettingsSection` is shared by Launcher Settings and setup, and appears only for BB10.
The current ordinary-install policy retains eight opened-app identities. Opening a ninth
replaces the oldest; summaries enrich matching cards without creating cards from historical
usage or incoming notifications. Calendar uses Hub-selected CalendarProvider calendars;
media matches session packages. Optional Hub excerpts and TenSeven Notes/Tasks/calculator
summaries respect their integration preferences. Office document linking has been removed.
The Widgets page remains separate. Capture consent is described below.

The UI workflow tests API 34 and 35, plus three responsive configurations. Its Hub regression
checks all ten actions at a narrow width and scrolls to each before exercising shortcuts.
Physical hardware acceptance remains distinct from emulator evidence.


### User-approved shared-screen preview

ScreenCaptureActivity requests fresh Android MediaProjection consent. The non-exported
ScreenCaptureService consumes a result once, starts its mediaProjection foreground
notification before obtaining projection, registers callbacks before creating one virtual
display, and resizes that display and ImageReader on captured-content changes.
ScreenCaptureState holds only the latest in-memory thumbnail; no consent or pixels are
persisted. The user-selected region is shown as a separate Shared screen card and is never
attributed to a recent task, package or profile. Home visibility freezes updates before
Home is drawn; lock, system revocation, Stop and process death end the session. A new
session always needs fresh consent. No audio is captured. Thumbnail dimensions/throttle
and Home/lock decisions are pure CapturePolicy logic. Physical consent and protected-screen
qualification are tracked in P2B_LIVE_CAPTURE_ACCEPTANCE.md.

## P2 engineering boundaries (2026-11-03)

The current source replaces the historical monolithic layout described above: SableStartScreen
is the navigation/composition host; HubPage, CommandScreen, AppsScreen, HomeAppGrid,
EditHomeScreen, AppPrivacyScreen, AppearanceScreen, HomeActionBar, HomeWidgets and
Bb10HomeChrome are separate presenters with immutable inputs and callbacks. Shared palette,
argument models, layout tokens and primitives have their own files.

LauncherRuntime owns inventory I/O, package/profile/privacy signals and their lifecycle cleanup;
InventoryCoordinator owns generation-based stale-result rejection. LauncherHomeState owns
Compose preference/session state. PlatformCapabilityState supplies lifecycle-refreshed typed
capabilities; HubRevision supplies a lifecycle-bound notification revision to inbox and Peek.

See P2_ENGINEERING_ACCEPTANCE.md for tests, accepted legacy static baseline, blocking quality
ratchet and the distinction between synthetic/emulator evidence and P3 hardware qualification.
P3 follows P2; KEY2 is removed from the active device list. The owner tests the Full APK once
both phases are delivered.

Owner scope update: Full APK minimum is Android 14 (API 34). P3 also includes Zinwa P26;
its OS, key events and display metrics remain to be captured. API-35 profile actions are
registered only behind an Android 15+ version guard. Emulator CI covers API 34 and 35.

### P3 device and widget boundaries

HomeViewport uses measured window/insets/text scale rather than device-model dimensions.
LauncherKeys owns standard Android fallback chords; DeviceCompatibility reports actual
input capabilities and offers an explicit foreground metadata probe. No OEM scan code
is guessed or globally intercepted. WidgetBinding/WidgetRecovery are pure transaction
and reconciliation policies; WidgetHostStore journals local pending setup/sizes before
Android UI. WidgetHostController validates stage/id/provider/profile before committing,
and WidgetAvailability clears hosted content outside resumed, unlocked Home.
Physical target qualification is tracked separately in P3_DEVICE_QUALIFICATION.md.

### L0 provider identity and qualification

The production URI remains content://io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.hubcounts/apps, with separate signature READ_HUB_COUNTS and WRITE_HUB_COUNTS permissions. Manifest applicationId placeholders and runtime package-derived URIs keep the L0 debug URI at content://io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.debug.l0.hubcounts/apps. Debug permission names use the same isolated application ID. Debug never claims production's provider or signing identity; production-signed Sable Watch does not authenticate to a debug-signed core merely by package-name matching.

Only package/count rows are returned. Notification access denial returns no cursor; insert/update/delete always reject writes. Count snapshots deduplicate observer notifications from Hub and lock-layer listeners; shutdown unregisters them. No Watch installation is required. Runtime signature enforcement and device behavior require Android instrumentation/owner acceptance; source integration is not device acceptance.

# Build

> **L0 is a development candidate, HOLD FOR MERGE.** This branch builds Launcher Core (:app), independent Phone (:phone), independent Calendar (:calendar), and shared :design. Debug core uses io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.debug.l0; companions use .phone.debug and .calendar.debug. Existing Full installations/data must remain untouched. Four other tools await extraction. No production companion signing or migration is qualified. See the L0 receipt and ADR-0001; build success does not waive quality, policy or device gates.

## L0 permanent development and release status

The authoritative development checkout is `~/Documents/projects/tenseven-launcher`,
on `feature/tenseven-l0-lean-launcher-core` until integration is qualified.
Use the existing wrapper and module output directories. No packaging step is required
to compile, test or assemble. Root/module `build/` directories keep their normal meaning.

Retained local files (Git ignored, unaffected by ordinary Gradle clean):

- `builds/development/<source-sha>/<retention-time>-<worktree-digest>/`: isolated debug APKs.
- `builds/release-candidates/<version>-<source-sha>/`: qualified internal artifacts only.
- `validation/<source-sha>/`: commands, reports, hashes and qualification receipts.
- `archives/`: immutable imported evidence, source patches and recovery packages.

After a normal successful debug build, optionally copy its existing outputs:

```bash
export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk"
python3 tools/retain-development-builds.py
```

This helper never recompiles, signs, installs or publishes. It verifies package identity,
debuggability and signatures, copies all three outputs into exclusive staging, verifies
hashes, then renames to a unique directory. It never overwrites an accepted candidate.
The manifest records commit/tree, complete worktree fingerprint/status, application IDs,
versions, build type, output times and signer/APK SHA-256. A dirty worktree is explicitly
identified; its base commit alone does not reproduce it. Retention does not confer PASS.
Store exact test commands/exits and source patches with the validation receipt.

### Channel boundaries

Development uses `.debug.l0` (Launcher), `.phone.debug` and `.calendar.debug`, with
debug signing. All remain independently installable; no companion is required for Home.
The provider authority and signature permission follow the installed application ID.
Production Sable Watch uses the canonical production authority/signature; a debug APK
does not authenticate as the production signer.

An optimized internal candidate needs isolated IDs, non-debuggable applications,
R8/resource shrinking and a test signer. The current approved configuration does **not**
provide that complete channel. Its exact additional protected-endpoint proposal requires
independent approval before implementation. Unsigned release APKs are analysis artifacts,
not installable candidates. Do not re-sign canonical production packages for internal testing.

The historical release instructions below describe **1.0.0 / versionCode 18**, not a
qualified 2.0 release. Do not run `tools/build-release.sh` for a different distributed
2.0 build, reuse distributed version codes or access production credentials during L0
qualification. Existing signing configuration and registered certificate remain unchanged.
Before production: approve companion identities/signing, assign unused version metadata,
prove data migration/rollback, complete security and device gates, then qualify the exact
signed artifacts. No automatic GitHub/Play publication is performed by retention.

Clean-install development qualification must not replace the installed Full Launcher.
Titan 2 installation requires owner approval for the exact isolated artifact hashes.
Keep the accepted installation/data in place; do not clear data or uninstall it as rollback.
Recovery source and evidence remain in `archives/`; original temporary worktrees remain
preserved. Real production upgrades and rollback are separate release gates.

The eight core Titan 2 areas were owner-accepted. Settings cleanup and BBOS7 Recent
still need owner acceptance. API35 focus/widget failures and landscape timeout remain
separate open gates. Local tests do not stand in for SonarCloud, CodeQL or device acceptance.
The inherited main-relative analyzer/suppression inventories remain blocking.

## 1. Host setup

JDK 17 (Temurin recommended) and the Android SDK with `platforms;android-36`, `platforms;android-37.0` and `build-tools;36.0.0`:

```bash
sdkmanager 'platforms;android-36' 'platforms;android-37.0' 'build-tools;36.0.0'
export ANDROID_HOME=/path/to/android-sdk     # or write sdk.dir=... into local.properties (not committed)
```

The first Gradle run downloads Gradle 9.9.1 (checksum pinned in `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties`),
Android Gradle Plugin 9.5.1, Kotlin 2.4.21, Lifecycle 2.10.0 and the Compose BOM 2026.02.01.
Launcher/design retain SDK 36; new Phone/Calendar modules compile and target SDK 37. All three application minSDKs remain 34. Lifecycle 2.10 is pinned for compatibility
because 2.11 requires SDK 37, which the CI SDK channel does not provide.

## 2. Build and test

```bash
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug                         # app/build/outputs/apk/debug/Tenseven-Launcher-debug.apk
./gradlew :phone:assembleDebug :calendar:assembleDebug # independently buildable companions
./gradlew :app:assembleRelease                       # R8-minified: Tenseven-Launcher-release.apk when signed (section 2a), else -release-unsigned.apk
./gradlew :design:testDebugUnitTest :app:testDebugUnitTest :phone:testDebugUnitTest :calendar:testDebugUnitTest
./gradlew :design:lintDebug :app:lintDebug :phone:lintDebug :calendar:lintDebug # reports in build/reports/lint-results-debug.*
./gradlew detekt ktlintCheck                         # reports in build/reports/detekt, build/reports/ktlint
./gradlew :design:koverXmlReportDebug :app:koverXmlReportDebug
bash tests/run.sh                                    # static checks; needs python3, optionally shellcheck and xmllint
```

L0 debug core ID is `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.debug.l0`, isolated from existing Full and older debug installations. Do not install on Titan 2 without owner approval.

### 2a. Signing a release build

Android installs only signed APKs. The build signs the release when it finds a key; the key stays on your computer.

```bash
# Official release keystore: ~/tenseven-release-2.jks (PKCS12), alias tenseven.
# It is already registered in Android Developer Console. Never regenerate or commit it.
```

Then give the build the key, in either of two ways:

- a file `keystore.properties` at the repository root (git-ignored), with absolute paths:

  ```properties
  storeFile=/Users/you/tenseven-release-2.jks
  storePassword=...
  keyAlias=tenseven
  keyPassword=...
  ```

- or environment variables `TENSEVEN_KEYSTORE`, `TENSEVEN_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `TENSEVEN_KEY_ALIAS`, `TENSEVEN_KEY_PASSWORD`.

```bash
./gradlew :app:assembleRelease
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/release/Tenseven-Launcher-release.apk
```

With signing credentials present, Gradle verifies the keystore certificate against the registered fingerprint before packaging. Older alpha APKs built before this certificate was created may not update in place; back up settings and reinstall if the signing identities differ. A different key fails closed. Without a key the build still succeeds and writes `Tenseven-Launcher-release-unsigned.apk` (what CI does). Use the same key
for every release: Android refuses to update an app signed with a different one. The release app id is
`io.github.aimindseye.tenseven` (no `.debug`), so it installs beside the debug build as a separate app.

### 2b. Mandatory Full-only signing and APK verification

The Lite variant is retired. A local Mac build with the *existing* registered keystore
produces one signed `Tenseven-Launcher-release.apk`; CI intentionally produces an unsigned
candidate and never receives signing secrets.

```bash
./gradlew :app:assembleRelease :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintRelease
python3 tests/test_release_verifier.py
bash tools/verify-release-apks.sh app/build/outputs/apk/release/Tenseven-Launcher-release.apk
```

For a complete local verified build and copied test package, use:
`bash tools/build-full-consolidated-test.sh`. The helper checks the release certificate and
delegates to `tools/build-release.sh` and writes versioned release files to
`~/Downloads/tenseven-release/1.0.0/`.

The registered release certificate SHA-256 is
`9b2047390e5aa77537b8e8875cdfd3c2c72d0a0715e172a7f77457fc4300f292`.
Never generate a replacement certificate or commit a signing key.
Android's sideload/restricted-settings checks still apply; no manifest can auto-approve
these privileged user choices.

## 2c. Version 1.0.0 on the owner’s Mac

Google uses manifest metadata, not a mandatory APK filename: `versionName = "1.0.0"`,
`versionCode = 18` (greater than the preceding code 17), and the unchanged application ID.
Before a Play upload, also confirm code 18 has not already been used for this application.
The Git tag is `v1.0.0`; the distribution APK is `TenSeven-Launcher-1.0.0.apk`.
The stable internal Gradle APK name is retained for existing automation.

After the release preparation PR has merged and its checks are green:

```bash
cd /Users/piyushdaiya/Documents/projects/tenseven-launcher
git switch main
git pull --ff-only origin main
export JAVA_HOME="$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17)"
export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk"
bash tools/build-release.sh
```

The helper requires clean tracked sources and the existing signing configuration. It runs
unit tests, release lint and the registered-key check, builds the signed APK, verifies its
compiled package/minSdk/version/signature, then copies the APK, checksum, release notes and
`SOURCE_COMMIT.txt` into `~/Downloads/tenseven-release/1.0.0/`. No manual signing command is needed.
`TENSEVEN_RELEASE_DIR` can override the output folder. Do not publish CI unsigned APKs.

Install and test the exact versioned asset:

```bash
adb install -r "$HOME/Downloads/tenseven-release/1.0.0/TenSeven-Launcher-1.0.0.apk"
```

## 2d. GitHub release after the signed build

Install/authenticate GitHub CLI (`brew install gh`, then `gh auth login`) if needed.
Publish only after testing the signed asset. Target the recorded source commit, so later
changes to main cannot change the release source:

```bash
cd /Users/piyushdaiya/Documents/projects/tenseven-launcher
release_dir="$HOME/Downloads/tenseven-release/1.0.0"
(cd "$release_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c TenSeven-Launcher-1.0.0.apk.sha256)
gh release create v1.0.0 \
  --repo aimindseye/tenseven-launcher \
  --target "$(cat "$release_dir/SOURCE_COMMIT.txt")" \
  --title "TenSeven Launcher 1.0.0" \
  --notes-file "$release_dir/RELEASE_NOTES.md" \
  "$release_dir/TenSeven-Launcher-1.0.0.apk" \
  "$release_dir/TenSeven-Launcher-1.0.0.apk.sha256" \
  "$release_dir/SOURCE_COMMIT.txt"
```

This creates the tag and release. If the tag/release already exists, inspect it first;
do not overwrite a published artifact or reuse its version code for a different build.

## 2e. Google Play bundle (separate distribution)

New Google Play applications require an Android App Bundle. A GitHub APK filename is not a
Play requirement. With the same signing configuration:

```bash
./gradlew --no-daemon :app:verifyRegisteredReleaseKey :app:bundleRelease
```

The AAB is under `app/build/outputs/bundle/release/`. The registered-key guard also runs for
release bundle signing. Confirm Play App Signing/upload-key configuration in Play Console
before uploading; APK verification does not verify an AAB or submit anything to Play.

Official references: [Android versioning](https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/versioning),
[Play app bundles](https://developer.android.com/guide/app-bundle).

## 3. Quality gates

detekt (rules: `config/detekt.yml`), ktlint (`.editorconfig`) and Android Lint **report without failing** while
`tenseven.strictQuality` is `false` (the default in `gradle.properties`). Compile errors and failing unit tests
always fail. The reason is honest and temporary: the imported SableOS sources were written under a different
rule baseline, and the gates have not yet been brought clean (`ROADMAP.md` phase 1).

To make the gates fail:

- locally: `./gradlew -Ptenseven.strictQuality=true detekt ktlintCheck :app:lintDebug`
- in CI: GitHub > Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > **Variables** > New repository variable
  `TENSEVEN_STRICT_QUALITY` = `true`

Do this once a run is clean. Anything kept on purpose goes in a detekt or Lint baseline with a reason, not in
a blanket suppression. `config/detekt.yml` is a byte-exact copy of SableOS's (checked by `tests/run.sh`
against `config/DETEKT_PROVENANCE.env`); put Tenseven's own rules in a second file and add it to `config.setFrom`
in `build.gradle.kts`.

## 4. Dependency locks and checksums

Not committed yet (`ROADMAP.md` phase 1): they need network access to write. On a machine with internet and the SDK:

```bash
bash tools/refresh-locks.sh
git add -A '*gradle.lockfile'
```

`build.gradle.kts` turns locking on for each module that has a `gradle.lockfile`, so nothing changes until you
commit them. After that, a changed dependency fails the build until the locks are refreshed on purpose.

## 5. Icons and brand logos

```bash
python3 tools/tabler_icons.py check          # manifest, SVGs and generated files agree (CI runs this)
python3 tools/tabler_icons.py import --from <extracted @tabler/icons package>   # after adding a glyph name
python3 tools/brand_assets.py check
python3 tools/brand_assets.py fetch          # on a machine with internet: Google Play listing icons
```

See `third_party/tabler-icons/PROVENANCE.md` and [`BRAND_ASSETS.md`](BRAND_ASSETS.md).

## 6. GitHub Actions

| Workflow | File | Runs on | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checks` | `.github/workflows/checks.yml` | PR and `main`, except docs-only | nothing |
| `Android` | `.github/workflows/android.yml` | PR and `main` when `app/`, `design/`, `config/`, `gradle/` or the Gradle files change | optional variable `TENSEVEN_STRICT_QUALITY` |
| `Security` | `.github/workflows/security.yml` | every PR, `main`, and Mondays | nothing |
| `CodeQL` | `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` | PR (code changes), `main`, and Mondays | nothing; code scanning must be enabled for the repository |
| `SonarCloud` | `.github/workflows/sonar.yml` | PR and `main` | secret `SONAR_TOKEN`; project `aimindseye_tenseven-launcher` in organisation `aimindseye` with Automatic Analysis **off** |

Actions are pinned by commit, as in SableOS; Dependabot proposes updates weekly. Pull requests from forks do
not get `SONAR_TOKEN`, so the SonarCloud job skips them.

The P2 quality ratchet is blocking for new findings even while global strict mode is off.
The Frames UI workflow runs API 34/35 instrumentation and three responsive configurations.
Sonar imports Kover coverage with the exclusions documented in `sonar-project.properties`.

### SonarCloud first-time setup

1. In SonarCloud, import `aimindseye/tenseven-launcher` into the `aimindseye` organisation. The project key must be
   `aimindseye_tenseven-launcher` (it is in `sonar-project.properties`).
2. Project > Administration > Analysis Method: turn **Automatic Analysis off**.
3. The repository secret `SONAR_TOKEN` must belong to a user who can analyse that project.
4. Run the workflow once from the Actions tab. Kover XML reports are imported by the workflow; retain the documented coverage exclusions and quality thresholds.

### What CI cannot do

Run on a phone, test the keyboard, or build a signed release. Those are manual and are tracked in
`ROADMAP.md`. A debug build goes onto a phone with `adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/Tenseven-Launcher-debug.apk`
(the Titan 2 shows as one adb device; the app id is `io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.debug`).

name: Security

# Gitleaks over the history and a MobSF source scan of the Android sources (findings recorded, not
# failing, as in SableOS).
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 5 * * 1'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: security-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  gitleaks:
    name: Gitleaks secret scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install Gitleaks 8.30.1
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          v=8.30.1
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSfL -o gl.tgz "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v$v/gitleaks_${v}_linux_x64.tar.gz"
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSfL -o sums.txt "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v$v/gitleaks_${v}_checksums.txt"
          grep " gitleaks_${v}_linux_x64.tar.gz\$" sums.txt | sed "s/gitleaks_${v}_linux_x64.tar.gz/gl.tgz/" | sha256sum -c -
          tar -xzf gl.tgz gitleaks && sudo install gitleaks /usr/local/bin/
      - name: Scan history
        run: gitleaks git --redact --no-banner --exit-code 1 .

  mobsfscan:
    name: MobSF Android source scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Scan
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pip install --quiet --require-hashes --only-binary :all: -r .github/requirements/mobsfscan.txt
          mobsfscan app design phone calendar --sarif --output mobsfscan-results.sarif --type android --no-fail
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import json, os
          doc = json.load(open("mobsfscan-results.sarif"))
          n = sum(len(r.get("results", [])) for r in doc.get("runs", []))
          print(f"MOBSFSCAN_SARIF_RESULT_COUNT={n}")
          with open(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"], "a") as f:
              f.write(f"MobSF findings recorded: **{n}**\n")
          PY
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: mobsfscan-results
          path: mobsfscan-results.sarif
          retention-days: 30

# L0 lean Launcher candidate

The Launcher Core, Phone and Calendar are independent development APKs. The
owner accepted all eight Titan 2 functional areas for source fingerprint
`bfa906a7a903ecc65e6e85ea93c4107496abd712accb845ba44cbd7c5f6814df`.
That acceptance covers the existing BBOS7/10 homes, notifications, Peek, lock
screen, keyboard/trackpad, Active Frames, widgets, Phone, Calendar and startup
without companions. It does not constitute acceptance of later source changes.

## Settings and BBOS7 Recent

Settings now has six numbered pages: Permissions, Appearance & Home, Hub, Lock
screen, Active Frames, and Review & Finish. Optional companion status is a
separate entry. The planner remains informational; it does not install APKs or
grant roles. Old Apps & Features links open companion status. Type to search
retains its existing preference under Appearance & Home; device compatibility
is under Permissions. Existing bundled-app choices remain stored for recovery
but no longer enable embedded Activities from Launcher Settings.

BBOS7's default panel order is Favorites, All, Recent, Downloads. Frequent is
separate and optional. Recent resolves locally recorded Launcher launches
against currently available personal-profile applications, newest first,
without requesting usage access. The existing Remember returned apps setting
disables both recording and Recent display. Disabling it does not silently
delete older records. Missing/uninstalled applications are omitted.

On first reading an older panel list, Recent is inserted before Downloads, or
after All, or at the end. Other saved order and disabled panels are preserved.
Saving records a trailing version marker so explicitly hiding Recent remains
effective. Older Launchers ignore that unknown marker. Reading alone does not
rewrite preferences. Touch, panel arrows, Space and Alt+Left/Right use the
existing tray controls; arrows/Enter use the existing grid navigation.

The two UI changes require Titan 2 acceptance: check six-page Back/Next and
old links, Type to search persistence, default and custom panel orders,
Recent hide/re-enable, launches and return refresh, uninstallation, empty
history, privacy opt-out, and physical keyboard/trackpad navigation. Emulator
and JVM evidence is retained in the local qualification deliverable. It is
not a substitute for these device checks or the full remote Frames matrix.

## Titan 2 technical references

- [Owner's device research](https://github.com/aimindseye/unihertz-titan2)
- [Titan 2 documentation](https://github.com/Serlk/titan2-docs)
- [Titan 2 tools research](https://github.com/Serlk/titan2-tools)
- [Titan 2 boot research](https://github.com/Serlk/titan2-boot)
- [Titan 2 TWRP research](https://github.com/Serlk/titan2-twrp)

These are technical references for device characteristics and keyboard research.
Launcher development uses public Android APIs and ordinary user-granted
permissions. Rooting, bootloader unlocking, flashing, and TWRP are neither
required nor authorized. No firmware tools or code are imported by this change.

## Integration and release holds

The source remains uncommitted until the exact four-module quality-policy
transition has independent approval and mandatory gates pass. Existing analyzer
and suppression inventories remain blocking; device acceptance does not waive
them. Production-signed Sable Watch interoperability, existing-user migration
and rollback, production release signing, and the separate Tasks, Notes,
Calculator and Profiles APKs remain separate release work. Do not replace an
existing signed Launcher or migrate its records using these development APKs.

def state(repo, commit):
    names = set(ENDPOINTS) | set(ANCHORS) | set(FIXTURES) | set(COPIES)
    raw = repo._read(["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", object_id(commit), "--", *sorted(names)])
    result = dict.fromkeys(names)
    for item in raw.split(b"\0"):
        if not item:
            continue
        metadata, name = item.decode().split("\t", 1)
        mode, kind, identifier = metadata.split()
        if mode != "100644" or kind != "blob" or name not in result:
            raise QualityError("Unexpected approved policy/fixture mode or type")
        result[name] = object_id(identifier)
    return result


def expected(repo, after):
    result = {name: pair["after" if after else "before"] for name, pair in ENDPOINTS.items()}
    result.update(ANCHORS)
    for name, digest in FIXTURES.items():
        original = repo.blob(BASE, name)
        if hashlib.sha256(original).hexdigest() != digest:
            raise QualityError("Frozen fixture endpoint differs")
        result[name] = legacy.blob_id(original)
    for name, digest in COPIES.items():
        raw = repo.blob(BASE, next(iter(FIXTURES)))
        if hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != digest:
            raise QualityError("Effective fixture source differs")
        result[name] = legacy.blob_id(raw) if after else None
    return result


def commits(repo, head):
    if not repo.ancestor(BASE, head):
        raise QualityError("L0 base is outside candidate ancestry")
    revision = BASE + ".." + object_id(head)
    values = repo._read(["rev-list", "--ancestry-path", "--reverse", revision, "--"]).decode().splitlines()
    return [BASE, *(object_id(value) for value in values)]


def direct(repo, commit):
    values = repo._read(["rev-list", "--parents", "-n", "1", object_id(commit), "--"]).decode().split()
    return values == [commit, BASE]


def history(repo, head, before, after):
    states = {commit: state(repo, commit) for commit in commits(repo, head)}
    if states[BASE] != before:
        raise QualityError("Immutable L0 base differs")
    if head == BASE:
        return None
    origins = [commit for commit, value in states.items() if direct(repo, commit) and value == after]
    if len(origins) != 1:
        raise QualityError("Need one single-parent joint origin directly after L0 base")
    origin = origins[0]
    if not repo.ancestor(origin, head):
        raise QualityError("Origin is outside candidate history")
    for commit, value in states.items():
        expected_state = java_variant(repo, commit, after) if repo.ancestor(origin, commit) else before
        if value != expected_state:
            raise QualityError("Policy or fixture history modified, partial or restored")
    return origin


def verify(repo, base):
    """Validate exact current bytes and every before/after ancestry state."""
    head = repo.head()
    base = repo.resolve(base)
    if not repo.ancestor(base, head):
        raise QualityError("Comparison base is outside ancestry")
    before, after = expected(repo, False), expected(repo, True)
    # Verify approved original R2.1 history all the way to the frozen L0 parent.
    harness_origin = legacy._harness_origin(repo, BASE)
    from quality_gate_ci_policy import verify_l0_controller, _L0_PATHS
    verify_workflow_inventory(repo)
    names = set(after) | set(_L0_PATHS)
    with legacy._source_snapshot(repo, names) as data:
        controller = verify_l0_controller(repo, base, legacy._source_snapshot, legacy.blob_id)
        current = {name: legacy.blob_id(data[name]) for name in after}
        if current != java_variant(repo, head, after):
            raise QualityError("Unknown, partial or modified joint endpoint/fixture")
        modules = {item.parent.name for item in repo.path.glob("*/build.gradle.kts")}
        if modules != MODULES:
            raise QualityError("Unapproved or missing Android module")
        origin = history(repo, head, before, after)
    if controller["origin"] != origin:
        raise QualityError("Module/controller origins differ")
    verify_workflow_inventory(repo)
    if {item.parent.name for item in repo.path.glob("*/build.gradle.kts")} != MODULES:
        raise QualityError("Module inventory changed during verification")
    if repo.head() != head:
        raise QualityError("Candidate HEAD changed")
    return {"status": "VERIFIED_EXACT_MODULE_TRANSITION", "base": BASE,
            "origin": origin, "verification_mode": "pre_commit" if origin is None else "immutable_origin",
            "r21_origin": harness_origin, "modules": sorted(MODULES)}



def mainline_active(repo, head):
    ancestors = set(repo._read(["rev-list", object_id(head), "--"]).decode().splitlines())
    return MAINLINE_ORIGIN in ancestors



def verify_mainline_java(repo, head):
    if not mainline_active(repo, head):
        return False
    values = repo._read(["rev-list", "--parents", "-n", "1", MAINLINE_ORIGIN, "--"]).decode().split()
    if values != [MAINLINE_ORIGIN, MAINLINE_PARENT]:
        raise QualityError("Mainline action update parent differs")
    for name, pair in MAINLINE_PROOF.items():
        if (repo.blob_id(MAINLINE_PARENT, name), repo.blob_id(MAINLINE_ORIGIN, name)) != pair:
            raise QualityError("Mainline action update endpoint differs")
    return True



def java_variant(repo, head, after):
    if not verify_mainline_java(repo, head):
        return after
    result = dict(after)
    result.update(MAINLINE_VARIANTS)
    return result


def verify_workflow_inventory(repo):
    expected = {name for name in ENDPOINTS.keys() | ANCHORS.keys() if name.startswith(".github/workflows/")}
    current = {name for name in repo.files() if name.startswith(".github/workflows/")}
    if current != expected:
        raise QualityError("Workflow inventory changed without an exact approval")


def active(repo):
    head = repo.head()
    known = repo.files()
    current = "tools/quality_gate_module_policy.py" in known
    ancestors = set(repo._read(["rev-list", object_id(head), "--"]).decode().splitlines())
    historical = False
    if BASE in ancestors:
        for commit in commits(repo, head):
            value = repo._read(["ls-tree", object_id(commit), "--", "tools/quality_gate_module_policy.py"])
            historical = historical or bool(value)
    if repo.head() != head:
        raise QualityError("HEAD changed while checking module activation")
    return current or historical



def modules(root):
    repo = GitRepository(root)
    names = {item.parent.name for item in root.glob("*/build.gradle.kts")}
    if active(repo):
        verify(repo, repo.head())
        return sorted(MODULES)
    if names != {"app", "design"}:
        raise QualityError("Module inventory changed without the exact L0 transition")
    return ["app", "design"]



def historical_records(repo, base, changed):
    verification = verify(repo, base)
    records = []
    for transition in legacy.TRANSITIONS:
        if transition.path not in changed:
            continue
        if (repo.blob_id(repo.parent(transition.origin), transition.path),
                repo.blob_id(transition.origin, transition.path)) != (transition.before, transition.after):
            raise QualityError("Historical transition endpoints differ")
        if not repo.ancestor(transition.origin, BASE):
            raise QualityError("Historical origin is outside frozen L0 parent")
        if repo.blob_id(base, transition.path) not in {
                transition.before, transition.after,
                ENDPOINTS.get(transition.path, {}).get("after")}:
            raise QualityError("Unknown historical comparison endpoint")
        records.append(legacy.asdict(transition))
    records.extend(harness_records(repo, base, verification))
    allowed = set(ENDPOINTS) | set(legacy.TEST_HARNESS_ENDPOINTS) | {t.path for t in legacy.TRANSITIONS}
    protected = changed & (legacy.QUALITY_CONFIG_FILES | set(ENDPOINTS))
    if protected - allowed:
        raise QualityError("Unapproved protected L0 configuration")
    workflows = {name for name in changed if name.startswith(".github/workflows/")}
    if workflows - set(ENDPOINTS):
        raise QualityError("Unapproved workflow transition")
    return records



def harness_records(repo, base, verified=None):
    verified = verify(repo, base) if verified is None else verified
    records = []
    for name, pair in legacy.TEST_HARNESS_ENDPOINTS.items():
        current = ENDPOINTS.get(name, {}).get("after", pair[1])
        previous = repo.blob_id(base, name)
        if previous not in {pair[0], pair[1], current}:
            raise QualityError("Unknown R2.1 comparison endpoint")
        records.append(dict(path=name, before=pair[0], after=current,
            original_after=pair[1], origin=verified["r21_origin"],
            origin_parent=legacy.TEST_HARNESS_BASE, comparison_base=base,
            comparison_base_blob=previous, verification_mode="immutable_origin",
            module_origin=verified["origin"], approval="Original R2.1 plus exact L0 source-set transition"))
    return records



def analysis(repo, parent):
    verified = verify(repo, parent.head())
    records = {item["path"]: item for item in harness_records(repo, parent.head(), verified)}
    for name in ("app/build.gradle.kts", "design/build.gradle.kts", "settings.gradle.kts"):
        previous = parent.blob_id(parent.head(), name)
        if name not in records:
            pair = ENDPOINTS[name]
            if previous not in {pair["before"], pair["after"]}:
                raise QualityError("Unknown L0 analysis input")
            records[name] = dict(path=name, comparison_base_blob=previous,
                                 after=pair["after"], origin=verified["origin"])
    result = {}
    for name, record in records.items():
        result[name] = legacy._harness_analysis_record(
            record, legacy.source_bytes(parent, name), legacy.source_bytes(repo, name))
    return result



def review_permission_contract(repo, base, audit):
    verified = verify(repo, base)
    contract = PHONE_CONTRACT
    original = repo.blob(BASE, contract["before_path"])
    method = contract["method"].encode()
    if (legacy.blob_id(original) != contract["before_blob"]
            or hashlib.sha256(method).hexdigest() != contract["method_sha256"]
            or original.count(method) != 1):
        raise QualityError("Frozen Phone role contract differs")
    if repo.line_origin(BASE, contract["before_path"], contract["before_line"]) != contract["actual_original_annotation_origin"]:
        raise QualityError("Original Phone annotation provenance differs")
    path = contract["after_path"]
    with legacy._source_snapshot(repo, {path}) as data:
        if (legacy.blob_id(data[path]) != ENDPOINTS[path]["after"]
                or data[path].count(method) != 1):
            raise QualityError("Reviewed Phone source/role contract differs")
    marker = '    @SuppressLint("MissingPermission")'
    approved, pending = [], []
    for item in audit:
        if (item["file"] == path and item["line"] == contract["before_line"]
                and item["text"] == marker
                and item["classification"] == "permission-contract-review-required"):
            approved.append({**item, "approval": "L0 exact Phone role-contract relocation",
                "result": "EXACT_REVIEWED_CONTRACT", "original_source_commit": BASE,
                "original_annotation_commit": contract["actual_original_annotation_origin"],
                "original_blob": contract["before_blob"], "candidate_blob": ENDPOINTS[path]["after"],
                "method_sha256": contract["method_sha256"], "module_origin": verified["origin"]})
        else:
            pending.append(item)
    if len(approved) > 1:
        raise QualityError("Duplicate reviewed Phone marker")
    return pending, approved

name: CodeQL

# GitHub code scanning for Kotlin. Results appear under Security > Code scanning. Needs no secrets.
# Documentation-only changes are skipped on pull requests; the weekly run catches new queries.
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'app/**'
      - 'design/**'
      - 'phone/**'
      - 'calendar/**'
      - 'gradle/**'
      - 'build.gradle.kts'
      - 'settings.gradle.kts'
      - 'gradle.properties'
      - '.github/workflows/codeql.yml'
      - '!**/*.md'
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '30 4 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: codeql-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  analyze:
    name: Analyze (java-kotlin)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
      actions: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
      - name: Android SDK 36 and 37
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sdkmanager="$(find "$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools" -type f -name sdkmanager -print -quit)"
          test -n "$sdkmanager"
          yes | "$sdkmanager" --licenses > /dev/null || true
          "$sdkmanager" 'platforms;android-36' 'platforms;android-37.0' 'build-tools;36.0.0'
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@3f5f9adaf7d9fecd50b5935e54106014257a94e6 # v6.4.0
        with:
          cache-read-only: true
      - name: Initialize CodeQL
        uses: github/codeql-action/init@0d579ffd059c29b07949a3cce3983f0780820c98 # v4
        with:
          languages: java-kotlin
          build-mode: manual
          queries: security-and-quality
      # CodeQL traces the compiler processes this step starts, so nothing may be skipped or run elsewhere:
      # no Gradle build cache or up-to-date skips (--rerun-tasks), no Gradle daemon, and the Kotlin compiler in
      # the Gradle process instead of the separate Kotlin daemon, which CodeQL cannot trace.
      - name: Build for CodeQL
        run: >-
          ./gradlew clean :design:compileDebugKotlin :app:compileDebugKotlin :phone:compileDebugKotlin :calendar:compileDebugKotlin
          --no-daemon --no-build-cache --no-configuration-cache --rerun-tasks --console=plain
          -Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process
      - name: Perform CodeQL analysis
        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@0d579ffd059c29b07949a3cce3983f0780820c98 # v4
        with:
          category: /language:java-kotlin

package io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.model

enum class ExtraGroup { Tools }

/** Optional-app metadata; [className] preserves legacy shortcut/icon identity, never installation trust. */
data class ExtraApp(
    val id: String,
    val label: String,
    val summary: String,
    val className: String,
    val glyph: AppGlyph,
    val group: ExtraGroup,
)

/**
 * The six optional companion choices. L0 builds Phone and Calendar separately; the other four await extraction.
 * Choices are informational and never hide ordinary installed Android apps. Pure policy, unit tested.
 */
object ExtraApps {
    private const val ROOT = "io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.extras."

    val ALL: List<ExtraApp> =
        listOf(
            ExtraApp(
                "tenseven_phone",
                "TenSeven Phone",
                "BlackBerry-style keypad and contacts with Android Phone handoff",
                "io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.features.phone.TenSevenPhoneActivity",
                AppGlyph.PHONE,
                ExtraGroup.Tools,
            ),
            ExtraApp(
                "tenseven_calendar",
                "TenSeven Calendar",
                "Month busy arcs, agenda and multiple synced calendars",
                "io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.features.calendar.TenSevenCalendarActivity",
                AppGlyph.CALENDAR,
                ExtraGroup.Tools,
            ),
            ExtraApp(
                "calculator",
                "Calc Plus",
                "Exact arithmetic, scientific functions and unit conversion",
                ROOT + "calculator.MainActivity",
                AppGlyph.CALCULATOR,
                ExtraGroup.Tools,
            ),
            ExtraApp(
                "tasks",
                "Tasks",
                "To-dos, due dates, repeating tasks and reminders; a separate app alongside Notes",
                "io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.tasks.TasksLauncherActivity",
                AppGlyph.TASKS,
                ExtraGroup.Tools,
            ),
            ExtraApp(
                "notes",
                "Notes",
                "Notes and checklists kept on the phone; share text into a new note",
                ROOT + "notes.MainActivity",
                AppGlyph.NOTES,
                ExtraGroup.Tools,
            ),
            ExtraApp(
                "profiles",
                "Sound Profiles",
                "BlackBerry sound profiles: Normal, Loud, Vibrate only, Phone calls only, All alerts off",
                ROOT + "profiles.MainActivity",
                AppGlyph.MEDIA,
                ExtraGroup.Tools,
            ),
        )

    private val byClass = ALL.associateBy { it.className }

    fun byClassName(className: String): ExtraApp? = byClass[className]

    fun isExtra(className: String): Boolean = className in byClass

    fun ofGroup(group: ExtraGroup): List<ExtraApp> = ALL.filter { it.group == group }

    /** Drops unknown ids; the default (nothing chosen) is the empty set. */
    fun normalize(ids: Collection<String>?): Set<String> = ids.orEmpty().filter { id -> ALL.any { it.id == id } }.toSet()

    /** What to switch on and off to move from [current] to [wanted], by id. */
    fun changes(
        current: Set<String>,
        wanted: Set<String>,
    ): Pair<Set<String>, Set<String>> {
        val target = normalize(wanted)
        val now = normalize(current)
        return (target - now) to (now - target)
    }
}

+package io.github.aimindseye.tenseven
+
+import android.content.ComponentName
+import android.content.ContentValues
+import android.content.pm.PermissionInfo
+import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry
+import io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.conversations.ConversationAccess
+import io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.platform.HubCountsProvider
+import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
+import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
+import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
+import org.junit.Assert.assertThrows
+import org.junit.Test
+
+/** Cross-UID denial is additionally tested from the isolated emulator shell. */
+class HubCountsContractInstrumentationTest {
+    private val context get() = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().targetContext
+    private val uri get() = HubCountsProvider.appsUri(context.packageName)
+
+    @Test
+    fun installedProviderIsIsolatedAndSignatureProtected() {
+        val manager = context.packageManager
+        val provider = manager.getProviderInfo(ComponentName(context, HubCountsProvider::class.java), 0)
+        assertEquals(context.packageName + ".hubcounts", provider.authority)
+        assertEquals(context.packageName + ".permission.READ_HUB_COUNTS", provider.readPermission)
+        assertEquals(context.packageName + ".permission.WRITE_HUB_COUNTS", provider.writePermission)
+        assertFalse(provider.grantUriPermissions)
+        for (permission in listOf(provider.readPermission, provider.writePermission)) {
+            val info = manager.getPermissionInfo(permission, 0)
+            val protection = info.protectionLevel and PermissionInfo.PROTECTION_MASK_BASE
+            assertEquals(PermissionInfo.PROTECTION_SIGNATURE, protection)
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun notificationAccessDenialProducesNoCursor() {
+        HubCountsAccessFixture().use { access ->
+            access.setGranted(false)
+            assertFalse(ConversationAccess.isGranted(context))
+            assertNull(context.contentResolver.query(uri, null, null, null, null))
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun evenTheOwnerCannotWriteCounts() {
+        val resolver = context.contentResolver
+        val values = ContentValues()
+        assertThrows(UnsupportedOperationException::class.java) { resolver.insert(uri, values) }
+        assertThrows(UnsupportedOperationException::class.java) { resolver.update(uri, values, null, null) }
+        assertThrows(UnsupportedOperationException::class.java) { resolver.delete(uri, null, null) }
+    }
+}

+/** Uses real resolver delivery while restoring the original notification-access state. */
+class HubCountsObserverInstrumentationTest {
+    @Test

+            verifyObserver()
+        }
+    }
+
+    private fun verifyObserver() {
+        val instrumentation = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
+        val context = instrumentation.targetContext
+        val uri = HubCountsProvider.appsUri(context.packageName)
+        val prior = LockLayerState.counts
+        val signal = CountDownLatch(1)
+        val observer =
+            object : ContentObserver(null) {
+                override fun onChange(
+                    selfChange: Boolean,
+                    changed: Uri?,
+                ) {
+                    if (changed == uri) signal.countDown()
+                }
+            }
+        context.contentResolver.query(uri, null, null, null, null)?.close()
+        context.contentResolver.registerContentObserver(uri, false, observer)

+                }
+            }
+            assertTrue(signal.await(OBSERVER_SECONDS, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
+        } finally {
+            context.contentResolver.unregisterContentObserver(observer)
+            instrumentation.runOnMainSync { LockLayerState.update(prior) }
+        }

+
+/** Clean-emulator startup checks; physical keyboard, roles and Titan 2 acceptance remain separate. */
+class L0CoreStartupInstrumentationTest {
+    @Test
+    fun bb7StartsWithoutWatchOrCompanions() = start(HomeStyle.Bb7)
+
+    @Test
+    fun bb10StartsWithoutWatchOrCompanions() = start(HomeStyle.Bb10)
+
+    @Test
+    fun launcherSettingsOpenIndependently() {
+        ActivityScenario.launch(LauncherSettingsActivity::class.java).use { scenario ->
+            scenario.onActivity { activity ->
+                assertFalse(activity.isFinishing)
+                assertNotNull(activity.window.decorView)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    private fun start(style: HomeStyle) {
+        val instrumentation = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
+        val context = instrumentation.targetContext
+        check(context.packageName == "io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.debug.l0")
+        val state = StartStateRepository(context)
+        val preferences = context.getSharedPreferences(StartStateRepository.PREFERENCES_NAME, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
+        val keys = listOf(StartStateRepository.KEY_HOME_STYLE, StartStateRepository.KEY_ONBOARDING_DONE)
+        val prior = preferences.all.filterKeys { it in keys }
+        try {
+            instrumentation.runOnMainSync {
+                state.saveOnboardingDone()
+                state.saveHomeStyle(style)
+            }
+            ActivityScenario.launch(SableStartActivity::class.java).use { scenario ->
+                scenario.onActivity { activity ->
+                    assertFalse(activity.isFinishing)
+                    assertNotNull(activity.window.decorView)
+                }
+            }
+        } finally {
+            val editor = preferences.edit()
+            for (key in keys) {
+                when (val value = prior[key]) {
+                    is String -> editor.putString(key, value)
+                    is Boolean -> editor.putBoolean(key, value)
+                    null -> editor.remove(key)
+                    else -> error("Unexpected preference type: $key")
+                }
+            }
+            check(editor.commit())
+        }
+    }

+// Derived from SableOS (github.com/aimindseye/zinwaq25-sableos @ 31420f599c2f,
+// sable-src/apps/r8/android/notes/src/main),
+// Apache License 2.0. Changed: package and imports renamed for Tenseven; native Rust calls replaced by Kotlin where
+// noted.
+package io.github.aimindseye.tenseven.extras.notes.core
+
+/**
+ * Checklist lines in a note's text: "- [ ] milk" is open, "- [x] milk" is done. The text stays
+ * plain, so an exported note reads the same in any editor.
+ */
+object Checklist {
+    const val OPEN = "- [ ] "
+    const val DONE = "- [x] "
+    private val ITEM = Regex("""^(\s*)- \[([ xX])] ?(.*)$""")
+
+    data class Item(
+        val indent: String,
+        val text: String,
+        val done: Boolean,
+    )
+
+    data class Progress(
+        val done: Int,
+        val total: Int,
+    )
+
+    /** An edit to the text: the new text and where the cursor goes. */
+    data class Edit(
+        val text: String,
+        val cursor: Int,
+    )
+
+    fun parse(line: String): Item? =
+        ITEM.matchEntire(line)?.let { match ->
+            val (indent, mark, text) = match.destructured
+            Item(indent, text, mark != " ")
+        }
+
+    fun progress(body: String): Progress {
+        val items = body.lineSequence().mapNotNull(::parse).toList()
+        return Progress(items.count { it.done }, items.size)
+    }
+
+    /** Ticks or unticks the item on line [line] (0-based); null when that line is not an item. */
+    fun toggleLine(
+        body: String,
+        line: Int,
+    ): String? {
+        val lines = body.split('\n').toMutableList()
+        val item = lines.getOrNull(line)?.let(::parse) ?: return null
+        lines[line] = item.indent + (if (item.done) OPEN else DONE) + item.text
+        return lines.joinToString("\n")
+    }
+
+    /** Ctrl+Enter: ticks or unticks the item under the cursor, keeping the cursor on its line. */
+    fun toggleAt(
+        body: String,
+        cursor: Int,
+    ): Edit? {
+        val line = lineIndex(body, cursor)
+        val text = toggleLine(body, line) ?: return null
+        return Edit(text, cursor.coerceIn(0, text.length))
+    }
+
+    /** Ctrl+T: turns the line under the cursor into an open item, or an item back into plain text. */
+    fun convertAt(
+        body: String,
+        cursor: Int,
+    ): Edit {
+        val start = lineStart(body, cursor)
+        val end = lineEnd(body, cursor)
+        val line = body.substring(start, end)
+        val item = parse(line)
+        val replaced =
+            if (item != null) {
+                item.indent + item.text
+            } else {
+                val indent = line.takeWhile { it == ' ' || it == '\t' }
+                indent + OPEN + line.substring(indent.length)
+            }
+        val delta = replaced.length - line.length
+        val text = body.substring(0, start) + replaced + body.substring(end)
+        return Edit(text, (cursor + delta).coerceIn(start, start + replaced.length))
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Enter at the end of an item starts the next open item, as list apps do; Enter on an empty item
+     * ends the list. Null when the cursor's line is not an item, so Enter types a plain newline.
+     */
+    fun newline(
+        body: String,
+        cursor: Int,
+    ): Edit? {
+        val start = lineStart(body, cursor)
+        val end = lineEnd(body, cursor)
+        return parse(body.substring(start, end))?.let { item ->
+            if (item.text.isBlank()) {
+                Edit(body.substring(0, start) + body.substring(end), start)
+            } else {
+                val insert = "\n" + item.indent + OPEN
+                Edit(body.substring(0, cursor) + insert + body.substring(cursor), cursor + insert.length)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fun lineIndex(
+        body: String,
+        cursor: Int,
+    ): Int = body.substring(0, cursor.coerceIn(0, body.length)).count { it == '\n' }
+
+    private fun lineStart(
+        body: String,
+        cursor: Int,
+    ): Int = body.lastIndexOf('\n', cursor.coerceIn(0, body.length) - 1) + 1
+
+    private fun lineEnd(
+        body: String,
+        cursor: Int,
+    ): Int = body.indexOf('\n', cursor.coerceIn(0, body.length)).let { if (it < 0) body.length else it }
+}

+    YELLOW(NoteColors.YELLOW, "yellow"),
+    ORANGE(NoteColors.ORANGE, "orange"),
+    RED(NoteColors.RED, "red"),
